title: A partner who seems confused
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in a GP practice. The practice manager tells you that Dr Morgan, one of the GP partners, has seemed confused in recent clinics, has missed appointments, and once couldn't remember a patient he'd seen earlier that day.

Dr Shah is the senior partner. The practice manager asks you what she should do.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Speak to Dr Morgan yourself about his memory.
options.brief: Better coming from a senior colleague.
options.detailed: A conversation is needed, but a junior raising this with a senior partner may not be appropriate.

options.text: Suggest she tells Dr Shah, the senior partner.
options.brief: Those responsible for the practice need to know.
options.detailed: A senior partner can speak to Dr Morgan and decide what to do, including protecting patients.

options.text: Report Dr Morgan to the GMC.
options.detailed: This may be a health issue that can be addressed locally.

options.text: Tell her it isn't your place to get involved.
options.detailed: You can advise her on who to speak to.

options.text: Discuss it with your GP supervisor.
options.brief: Your supervisor can advise and may act.
options.detailed: This is a serious concern, and your supervisor can help.

options.text: Encourage her to note what she has observed.
options.brief: Clear facts help those who need to act.
options.detailed: Dates, missed appointments and specific incidents, recorded factually and without speculation, help the senior partner understand the concern and act fairly.

options.text: Suggest she checks Dr Morgan's notes for errors.
options.detailed: Reviewing clinical notes isn't her role, and should be done by a clinician.

options.text: Suggest she waits to see if it gets worse.
options.brief: Patients may be at risk now.
options.detailed: Waiting could put patients at risk.

explanation.issue: This tests how you respond to concerns about a senior colleague's health that may affect patients.
explanation.keyDetails: The concerns are specific. Dr Morgan is a senior partner. Patients may be at risk.
explanation.reasoning: [B] directs her to the right person, [E] involves your supervisor, and [F] helps make sure the concern is clear and fair. The distractors are inappropriate for your role ([A], [G]), premature ([C]), or dismissive ([D], [H]).
explanation.competing: [A] is the tempting option, but this conversation is better coming from a senior colleague.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 3, acting when a colleague's health may put patients at risk.

references.title: Raising and acting on concerns about patient safety
